description: SIW-R is serialized IW whose subgoals come from a *policy sketch* instead of the goal count. A sketch is a set of rules `C ↦ E` over Boolean and numerical state features: from a state that meets the conditions `C`, any other state whose features changed as the effects `E` allow is a subgoal, and every feature that no effect names must keep its value. From the current state, IW(1), IW(2), … up to `max_k` run until they reach a goal or such a subgoal; the single rule `{#g > 0} ↦ {#g↓}` gives SIW. SIW-R gives up when no subgoal is within width `max_k`, and when it reaches a subgoal state it passed before, since the sketch then cycles. Use it when you can write down how a domain splits into steps of low width, such as "pick up a key, then open the door".

papers.title: General Policies, Representations, and Planning Width
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

papers.authors: Dominik Drexler, Jendrik Seipp, Hector Geffner
papers.title: Expressing and Exploiting the Common Subgoal Structure of Classical Planning Domains Using Sketches
